entries.title: OFAC designates Egyptian and Jordanian Muslim Brotherhood branches as SDGTs
entries.summary: On 13 January 2026, the US Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated the Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood and the Jordanian Muslim Brotherhood as Specially Designated Global Terrorists under Executive Order 13224, as amended. Treasury stated the action targeted branches that provided material support to Hamas. The designation enables US asset freezes and transaction prohibitions for US persons dealing with the designated entities. Concurrent State Department action addressed the Lebanese Muslim Brotherhood chapter in a separate entry on the same day. Primary source: Treasury press release sb0357.

linkedActors.name: Hamas
linkedActors.relation: Material support rationale under E.O. 13224 (as stated in Treasury release)

linkedActors.name: US Department of the Treasury / OFAC

entries.title: State designates Lebanese Muslim Brotherhood as FTO and SDGT
entries.summary: On 13 January 2026, the US Department of State designated the Lebanese Muslim Brotherhood (also known as al-Jamaa al-Islamiyah) as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) and as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT). State also designated Secretary General Muhammad Fawzi Taqqosh as an SDGT. The action was announced concurrently with Treasury designations of the Egyptian and Jordanian Muslim Brotherhood branches. FTO listing carries immigration and material-support criminal consequences under US law, in addition to financial restrictions. Primary source: State Department announcement concurrent with the January 2026 MB package.

entries.amountNote: Blocking of property and interests in property of designated persons subject to US jurisdiction (amount not quantified in announcement).
entries.title: OFAC SDN list update — MB branches blocked under CT authorities
entries.summary: OFAC published SDN List updates adding Egyptian, Jordanian, and related Muslim Brotherhood listings under SDGT (and FTO for the Lebanese chapter via State), implementing asset blocking for US persons and US jurisdiction property.

entries.title: Terrorist designation of the Sudanese Muslim Brotherhood
entries.summary: In March 2026, US counterterrorism designation records included action related to the Sudanese Muslim Brotherhood, continuing the 2026 campaign against Muslim Brotherhood chapters framed as SDGT-related terrorist designations. The ledger records the official designation update as published in OFAC Recent Actions / counterterrorism designation lists. As with all ledger rows, the legal effect is limited to what the primary US government instrument states; this is not an independent finding of guilt against unnamed affiliates. Primary source: OFAC Recent Actions / State-Treasury designation packaging for Sudanese MB.

entities: Hayat Yolu (Türkiye-based, referenced as MB financial hub)
entries.title: OFAC designates sham charities funding Hamas military wing
entries.summary: On 12 March 2026, the US Treasury announced designations of four organizations it described as sham charities that directly fund Hamas’s military wing, the Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades. The release also referenced Türkiye-based Hayat Yolu as an operational headquarters and banking or financial hub for Muslim Brotherhood–related activity connected to the package. Designations under E.O. 13224 block property and interests in property of the designated parties that come within US jurisdiction and prohibit US persons from dealing with them. Linked NGOs and charities appear only as named in the Treasury release. Primary source: Treasury press package on Hamas financing / sham charities.

entries.title: UAE State Security dismantles Hezbollah/Iran-funded terror network
entries.summary: On 19 March 2026, the UAE State Security Apparatus publicly announced that it had dismantled a terrorist network funded and operated by Hezbollah and Iran. Authorities stated that members of the network were arrested and that the group had operated under fictitious commercial cover while seeking to infiltrate the national economy. The announcement is a primary UAE security statement; individuals remain subject to UAE legal process. This ledger row captures the official arrest/network-dismantling claim and the named state sponsors as stated by UAE authorities. Primary source: UAE State Security / official UAE media relay of the SSA announcement.

source.label: WAM / official UAE State Security announcement (via WAM English)

entries.amountNote: Treasury stated the network enabled diversion of over $100 million since 2020 (estimate in official release).
entries.title: OFAC sanctions Alaa Hamieh global network diverting funds to Hezbollah
entries.summary: On 20 March 2026, OFAC designated a network of 16 individuals and entities led by Alaa Hassan Hamieh, described by Treasury as a Hezbollah financier and former Lebanese public investment official. Treasury stated that companies spanning Lebanon, Syria, Poland, Slovenia, Qatar, and Canada were used to launder and raise funds for Hezbollah’s finance team. The package is one of the largest quantified multi-jurisdiction Hezbollah finance actions in this ledger phase and anchors both US and Europe geography pins. Property and interests of designated parties under US jurisdiction are blocked. Primary source: Treasury press release sb0420.

entries.title: UAE Local Terrorist List: 16 individuals + 5 entities over Hezbollah links
entries.summary: In May 2026, the UAE Cabinet adopted Resolution No. (63) of 2026 adding 16 Lebanese nationals and five Lebanon-based entities to the UAE Local Terrorist List over alleged links to Hezbollah, as reported by the official Emirates News Agency (WAM). Entities publicly associated with the action include al-Qard al-Hassan and related companies. Local Terrorist List listing triggers UAE domestic counter-terror finance and association controls as defined under UAE law. This row records the Cabinet list action as a Gulf enforcement package parallel to US/TFTC Hezbollah finance pressure. Primary source: WAM / UAE Cabinet resolution coverage.

source.label: WAM / Gulf News official cabinet reporting

entries.title: SDNY charges Iraqi operative with material support to IRGC and Kata’ib Hizballah
entries.summary: On 15 May 2026, the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York announced the arrest and federal charges against Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, alleged to be a senior member of Kata’ib Hizballah. The government charged material support to Kata’ib Hizballah and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and related terrorism offenses. Charges are allegations until adjudicated in court. The case is recorded here as an IRGC / Iraq militia axis enforcement action with primary DOJ sourcing. Primary source: SDNY / DOJ press release on the Al-Saadi arrest and indictment.

entries.title: TFTC joint designations: Hezbollah financial institutions and senior officials
entries.summary: On 30 June 2026, the Terrorist Financing Targeting Center (TFTC)—co-chaired by the United States and Saudi Arabia and including GCC member states—announced joint designations targeting key Hezbollah financial infrastructure. The package publicly emphasized Al-Qard Al-Hassan and Bayt al-Mal among five entities and 16 individuals. TFTC actions are coordinated multilateral designations by member authorities; national legal instruments still govern freezes in each jurisdiction. Gulf co-chair and member pins (Riyadh, Manama, etc.) support the geographic story of the same package. Primary source: TFTC / Treasury joint announcement for Round 9 Hezbollah finance designations.

entries.title: OFAC designates Mahmoud al-Abyari + Hamas/MB financial facilitators
entries.summary: On 23 July 2026, OFAC designated UK-based senior Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood official Mahmoud al-Abyari, identified as Secretary General of the MB General Secretariat, for acting on behalf of the Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood. The same package designated three individuals and three entities for providing material support to Hamas. Treasury cited support for previously sanctioned Filistin Vakfi and Hayat Yolu and described MB-linked fundraising channels for Hamas. A London geographic pin marks al-Abyari’s UK base as stated by Treasury. Primary source: Treasury press release sb0572.

entries.title: Treasury sanctions Hezbollah financial officials tied to Al-Qard Al-Hassan
entries.summary: OFAC sanctioned Hezbollah financial officials who served in senior management roles for Al-Qard Al-Hassan (AQAH), a Hezbollah-linked financial institution previously designated in 2007. Builds the public record for later TFTC joint AQAH targeting.

entries.amountNote: Trial evidence cited nearly $100,000,000 moved by co-conspirators in less than 18 months (not all attributed solely to listed networks).
entries.title: EDVA jury convicts Lebanese-Syrian national in narco-terrorism / material support case
entries.summary: Federal jury in EDVA convicted dual Lebanese-Syrian national Antoine Kassis on narco-terrorism conspiracy and conspiracy to provide material support to a designated FTO. Court records cited large-scale money movement involving organizations including Hamas among others. Conviction is a court outcome; read full DOJ release for charges and evidence summary.

entries.title: Germany bans Hezbollah activity nationwide (all branches)
entries.summary: On 30 April 2020, Germany prohibited all Hezbollah activity on its territory, covering political and social branches that had previously been treated differently from the military wing. The Federal Ministry of the Interior framed the ban as a national security measure against an organization responsible for terrorism abroad and for radicalization infrastructure in Europe. The ban enables association, activity, and related financial enforcement under German law. This ledger row records the public ban as a European enforcement baseline for later financial and association cases involving Hezbollah in Germany. Primary source: German Federal Ministry of the Interior press release (English).

source.label: German Federal Ministry of the Interior — Hezbollah ban (public reporting of official ban)

linkedActors.name: German Federal Ministry of the Interior

entries.title: United Kingdom proscribes Hezbollah in full
entries.summary: In February 2019, the United Kingdom extended terrorism proscription to cover Hezbollah in its entirety, not only the military wing. Full proscription makes membership of and support for the organization offences under UK terrorism legislation. The Home Office cited Hezbollah’s involvement in terrorism and the impracticality of separating political and military wings for enforcement purposes. Proscribed-organisation status is a foundational UK legal tool for subsequent association, fundraising, and related prosecutions. Primary source: UK Home Office proscribed terrorist groups publication / related Home Office materials.

source.label: UK Home Office — Proscribed terrorist groups

entries.title: EU lists Hezbollah military wing as a terrorist organization
entries.summary: The Council of the European Union decided to add the military wing of Hezbollah to the EU list of terrorist organizations and persons, enabling asset freezes and other restrictive measures under the EU counter-terrorism framework. Member states retain national tools alongside the EU listing. This ledger row records the EU-level listing as a foundational European designation that underpins later financial enforcement and national measures across the Union. Coordinates are placed on Brussels as the seat of the Council decision-making process. Primary source: Council of the EU press materials / official listing framework documents.

source.label: Council of the EU — Hezbollah military wing listing (2013)
